title: Erin

pages.message: The storm's powerful winds churn up ocean water, creating sea salt particles visible as blue spirals.
This visualization still image highlights how our atmosphere connects distant parts of the world.

note: Ours: the two weeks around EIC's still, every 3 hours. The view centre is Erin's eye, from the NHC best track. Each particle type is a stem: its amount is the AOD over the visible half of the globe, weighted cos⁴ towards the view centre; its position is the AOD-weighted centre in degrees from the view centre; its speed is total mass flux over total mass. The event columns follow one plume from its source to a distant receptor (section 9.4): sea salt from Erin's eye, spreading, threshold AOD 0.15; dust from the Sahara to Erin's eye, threshold AOD 0.2.

sources.source: NASA GMAO GEOS-FP, tavg3_2d_aer_Nx (3-hourly 2-D aerosol diagnostics, 0.25° × 0.3125°)
sources.version: GEOS-FP as run in August 2025 (operational, upgraded in place)
sources.credit: Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO), NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
sources.substitute: EIC cites the GEOS-FP 2 km Replay, which has no download. GEOS-FP is the same model at 0.25°, public over HTTPS.

sources.source: NOAA National Hurricane Center best track, Erin (AL05 2025), ATCF b-deck
